subject: Commit uplift & rateband alignment for Fabrik Labs – proposed cadence
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tharris@fabriklabs.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@fabriklabs.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: hosted API commit increases & rateband questions

Hi Ava,

Quick note from our side — traffic on a core recommendation endpoint has grown 3x in the last quarter and we’re planning to scale more aggressively in Q4. We currently have a hosted commit of ~2,000,000 tokens / month and are evaluating a jump toward ~6,000,000 tokens/month (with headroom for short spikes).

Before we book more time I wanted to clarify a few things you can share briefly by email:
- How does ratebanding change across commit tiers? Will per-token price step down automatically at 4M / 6M, or do we need an amendment?
- If we ramp across 3 months (2M -> 4M -> 6M), what throttling/softburst protections do you recommend to avoid transient 429s?
- Can we pin a model version for the hosted API (we need deterministic output for a gated rollout)?

We’re on a tight procurement cadence — if we can get an ops-friendly ramp plan + indicative pricing I can loop legal and procurement. Available for a quick sync Thurs or Fri PST.

Thanks,
Tom Harris
Director of Product
Fabrik Labs
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.inference>
To: Tom Harris <tharris@fabriklabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: hosted API commit increases & rateband questions

Tom — great to hear about the growth, congrats to the team. Short answers up top, then a proposed plan below.

Quick answers:
- Ratebands: we provide tiered per-token pricing tied to committed monthly tokens. For your example we’d put a formal amendment to move you to the 6M band; however we can enable step-pricing for the first 90 days so you get the reduced unit price as you ramp (no retroactive credits).
- Throttling/softburst: recommend enabling a softburst pocket (10% of commit) for the first 60 days + adaptive request-smoothing on the client side. On our end we’ll configure a mixed-candidate routing policy so requests above your commit hit a cheaper compatible model variant rather than returning a 429 during brief spikes.
- Model pinning: yes — hosted API supports pinning to a model version and we’ll surface an immutable model id in the call metadata.

Proposed uplift cadence (ops + commercial summary):
1) Month 1 (onboarding): commit change to 4M tokens, enable softburst 10%, set autoscale burst to 1.5x baseline.
2) Month 2 (observability): move to 5M tokens, run a controlled canary (1% traffic) pinned to the target model, evaluate latency/cost.
3) Month 3 (full): commit to 6M tokens, formal amendment signed, apply 6M rateband pricing.

Attached: fabrik_uplift_plan_v1.pdf (detailed schedule) and redwood_rateband_table.csv (illustrative pricing). Ben will follow up with the ops checklist and an onboarding timeline.

If Thurs 10:30am PST or Fri 09:00am PST works I’ll book 30m and bring Karthik and Ben.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive — Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Tom Harris <tharris@fabriklabs.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: hosted API commit increases & rateband questions

Tom — looping in some operational details you can share with your infra team. See inline suggestions below (keeps things practical for a staged ramp).

On Wed, 8 Sep 2027 at 11:05, Ava Chen wrote:
> Proposed uplift cadence (ops + commercial summary):
> 1) Month 1 (onboarding): commit change to 4M tokens, enable softburst 10%, set autoscale burst to 1.5x baseline.

Operational notes:
- Autoscale policy: set a conservative worker warm-up to avoid cold-start latency. We recommend target p95 end-to-end < 200ms for recommendation endpoints; the runtime will do continuous batching to hit throughput goals.
- Prefix/KV caching: enable request-prefix caching for repeated prompts — for recommendation lookups this reduces token counts on common calls by ~18% in our benchmarking.
- Monitoring hooks: we’ll provide per-route token breakdowns and a short eval harness to detect hallucination/regression during the canary.

I attached an ops_onboarding_checklist.xlsx with the required firewall rules, sample prom/Datadog alerts, and the kickoff runbook. For DocuSign and final pricing we’ll hand off to Ava — but from an SRE perspective the 2->4->6 ramp with a 10% softburst is safe if you adopt the caching + smoothing recommendations above.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ops_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (firewall rules, alerts, runbook)
